history.dynasty: Folk tradition; historically supported by the Chantan family
history.period: Folk origin, traditional; Theyyam rituals performed every day through the year
history.summary: The principal Muthappan shrine of the Theyyam tradition on the banks of the Valapattanam river at Parassinikkadavu, ~20 km north of Kannur. This is not a conventional temple but a madappura: there is no consecrated idol of the presiding deity. Instead, ritual artists embody Muthappan twice daily in Theyyam — the elaborate Thiruvappana (Vishnu aspect) and the minimalist Vellattam (Shiva aspect) — and devotees receive personal audience and blessings from the oracle. Legend: a baby found floating in a basket on the river was raised by the Brahmin lady Padikutty of Ayyankara as a blessing of Shiva; he revealed his Viswaroopam when admonished for his hunter's ways, and was named Muthappan by the tribal family he then lived with. Uniquely among Kerala temples, it is open to all castes, creeds and religions, and free meals are served at noon and evening. CSV town/state (Kannur, Kerala) are correct.

name: Parassinikkadavu Muthappan Temple
town_description: Parassinikkadavu is a riverside pilgrim town in Kannur district on the Valapattanam river, famous across Kerala and abroad for the Muthappan Theyyam performed daily at the Madappura.
tradition: Theyyam folk tradition; Dravidian folk Hinduism — Muthappan is a syncretic Shiva–Vishnu folk deity

travel.railway: Kannur railway station (~16–20 km); local buses from Kannur every ~30 min
travel.road: Parassinikkadavu–Mayyil road, on the Valapattanam river bank

visitor_information.best_time: October–May, especially February (Thiruvappana Mahotsavam); attend a morning or evening Theyyam
